label: Intercom
terms_note: Automation allowed with an access token (private app) or OAuth (public app): base https://api.intercom.io (EU https://api.eu.intercom.io, AU https://api.au.intercom.io), Authorization: Bearer, Intercom-Version header (2.16 documented). Rate limits: 10,000 API calls per minute per app and 25,000 per minute per workspace, distributed into 10-second windows; X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset (epoch); HTTP 429. Reply: POST /conversations/{id}/reply {message_type comment, type admin|user, admin_id, body (HTML for notes), attachment_urls ≤10, attachment_files ≤10, reply_options, created_at, skip_notifications}. Search: POST /conversations/search (operators = != IN NIN > < ~ !~ ^ $, ≤2 nesting levels, ≤15 filters per group, per_page ≤150, starting_after cursor). Webhook topics conversation.user.created / conversation.user.replied / conversation.admin.replied.

tools.name: send
tools.endpoint: POST /messages (new outbound conversation, in_app or email)

endpoints.call: POST /conversations/{id}/reply` `{message_type: comment, type: admin, admin_id, body, attachment_urls[≤10], attachment_files[≤10], reply_options, created_at, skip_notifications}
endpoints.notes: `id` may be `last`; body HTML allowed for notes

endpoints.purpose: OR, value[{field, operator, value}]}, pagination{per_page ≤150, starting_after}}`

reference.limits: - **10,000 API calls / minute per app**, **25,000 / minute per workspace**, enforced in 10-second windows; `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset` (epoch); HTTP 429 with `Remaining: 0`. - Errors `{type: error.list, errors[{code, message}]}`. Automation is the product's purpose (support inbox); Intercom Developer Terms.

fields.name: access_token
fields.help: Access Token of the app (Developer Hub > Configure > Authentication, or an OAuth install), sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>' (https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication). Workspaces hosted in the EU / AU are served from https://api.eu.intercom.io / https://api.au.intercom.io (OpenAPI servers list), which this server does not switch to.

config_fields.name: admin_id
config_fields.help: Intercom id of the admin (teammate) who authors replies and outbound messages — 'admin_id: The id of the admin who is authoring the comment' (https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/conversations/replyconversation); GET /me (the `me` tool) shows the token's own admin id. Env: PLATFORM_MCP_INTERCOM_ADMIN_ID.

adapter.headers_note: The optional Intercom-Version header is not sent: 'By default, it's equal to the version set in the app package' (https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/conversations/replyconversation); mappings follow API version 2.16.
adapter.rate_note: '10,000 API calls per minute per app' and '25,000 API calls per minute per workspace', spread over 10-second windows and reported in X-RateLimit-Limit / -Remaining / -Reset; HTTP 429 when exceeded (https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/errors/rate-limiting). Client bucket kept at a conservative 10/s.

me.note: 'You can view the currently authorised admin along with the embedded app object' — account carries type admin, id, name, email, email_verified and app{id_code, name, region}.

send.note: Admin-initiated in-app message ('You can create a message that has been initiated by an admin'): `to` is the contact's Intercom id ('The identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom') with role `user` — leads (recipient type lead) cannot be addressed; `from` is the per-install admin_id; message_type is fixed to in_app, so `subject` and `channel` are ignored (email messages also need template + subject). `text` is `body`, 'HTML and plaintext are supported'. UNCONFIRMED: the OpenAPI types from.id as an integer while the runtime sends the config value as a string. The result is the Message (id, conversation_id, body under raw); 'there will be no conversation present until the contact responds'.

reply.note: Public admin comment (message_type comment, type admin, admin_id from the per-install config): `thread_id` is the conversation id 'or the string "last" to reply to the last part of the conversation'; `channel` is ignored. The response is the whole Conversation (under raw); message_id is not set because the new part is only identifiable as the last entry of raw.conversation_parts.conversation_parts.

list_inbound.note: 'You can fetch a list of all conversations' — one row per conversation: `id` = `thread_id` = conversation id, `text` is the source (opening) message body (HTML), `from` its author's email (author object under raw.source.author). Intercom pages by cursor (pages.next.starting_after), so `page` is ignored and only the first `limit` (per_page, 'default 20', max 150) conversations are returned — next_page is not meaningful; `since` and `channel` are not sent (filters need POST /conversations/search, not offered). created_at / updated_at are Unix seconds under raw; total is raw.total_count on the response (not mapped).

get_thread.note: 'You can fetch the details of a single conversation' with display_as=plaintext ('Set to plaintext to retrieve conversation messages in plain text'): rows are the conversation parts (comments, notes, assignments... — part_type under raw), `from` is the part author's email (author under raw.author). The opening message is NOT a part (it is the conversation's source, see list_inbound). The endpoint has no paging parameters, so `limit`, `page` and `channel` are ignored; Intercom returns at most the 500 most recent parts. created_at is Unix seconds under raw.

mark_read.note: PUT /conversations/{id} with `read: true` — 'Mark a conversation as read within Intercom' (a JSON boolean, sent as such). `thread_id` is the conversation id and is required; `message_id` and `channel` are not used (Intercom tracks read state per conversation). The response is the updated Conversation (under raw).

evidence: probe: 6/6 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
